sentences.text: Ms.Sushma Bairagy - Advocate for the appellants.

Shri Ajay Shukla - Public Prosecutor for the respondent Heard on I.A.No.5850 of 2026, which is the first application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant No.1 - Ajay @ Ajju @ Satyaprakash Kaurav S/o Shri Chhattar Singh Kaurav.

The appellant No.1 is aggrieved of the judgment dated 27.02.2018, passed by the learned Special Judge (SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities), Act) Narsinghpur, District Narsinghpur (M.P.), in Special Case No.64 of 2016, whereby the appellant No.1 stands convicted and sentenced as under:-

sentences.text: who had not found any injury on any part of the body including the private part.
There was no redness and no bleeding.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix herself has admitted two facts which are important in deciding this application for suspension of sentence.

Firstly, after violation of privacy by two of the accused persons, she became unconscious but she has not taken the names of those two accused persons who had violated her privacy while she was conscious.

Secondly,
prosecutrix has admitted that relatives of the appellant had eloped with her bua about one and a half year back and there was enmity between the two families on account of such elopement of her bua.

Thus, it is submitted that when the violation of privacy in the hands of four persons is not medically supported especially the scene of crime which is said to be an open field and there is an old enmity between the families of the appellant and the prosecutrix on account of elopement of her bua, it is a fit case to grant the benefit of suspension of sentence to appellant No.1 on the ground of parity.
Ms. Sushma Bairagi, learned counsel for the appellants, further submits that appellant No.1 is a kidney patient; therefore, a prayer has been made for waiver of the fine amount.
Shri Ajay Shukla, learned Public Prosecutor, in his turn, opposes the prayer and submits that no interference is called for in the impugned judgment.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the 3 CRA-4613-2018 record so also looking to the fact that the appeal is going to take time for its disposal, without commenting on the merits of the case, we are of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant No.1 and to release him on bail on the ground of parity.

Hence, prayer for suspension of sentence is allowed, but prayer for waiving of fine amount or relaxation in depositing the fine amount, on account of the fact that appellant No.1 Ajay @ Ajju @ Satyaprakash Kaurav being a kidney patient is not supported by any documentary evidence, is hereby rejected.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only), with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 13.05.2026 and such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence imposed upon the present appellant No.1 - Ajju @ Ajay @ Satyaprakash Kaurav shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
I.A. No.5850/2026 is allowed & disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.
List for final hearing in Part-B of the cause list as per its turn and seniority.
